Achterberg⟧ but ive never actually met him, everything went through the agents

Assistant: Of course. Your strongest evidence is the check-in inventory, so the letter leads with it. Here's a draft you can paste into an email or print and post:

---

⟦name|Priya Raghunathan-Cole⟧
⟦street address|58 Cranbrook Rise
Ilford
IG1 3QW⟧
⟦phone number|07723 418095⟧ · ⟦email address|priya.rcole@fastmail.co.uk⟧

14 October 2026

⟦name|Gareth Pryce-Lewis⟧
Hollins & Barr Lettings
By email: ⟦email address|gareth.pl@hollinsbarr.co.uk⟧

Dear Mr ⟦name|Pryce-Lewis⟧,

**Re: Proposed deposit deductions – ⟦street address|Flat 3, 27 Wellesley Road, London E11 4HJ⟧ (your ref. DR-2026-11873)**

I am writing in response to your email of 9 October 2026 proposing deductions of £640 from my deposit of £1,750. I do not agree to these deductions, for the reasons set out below.

1. Carpet, second bedroom – £410
The staining you describe is recorded in the check-in inventory dated 2 September 2023 (photograph 14). As it was present at the start of the tenancy, it cannot be attributed to me. Even where damage does occur, a landlord is not entitled to betterment: a carpet that was already several years old at check-in would have little residual value after a further three years of fair wear and tear.

2. Professional cleaning – £230
The property was cleaned thoroughly before I returned the keys on 31 August 2026. I have date-stamped photographs of every room, which I am happy to provide. The check-out report does not identify any specific area that falls below the standard recorded at check-in.

I would therefore ask you to authorise the release of the full £640 within 14 days of this letter. If we cannot reach agreement, I will refer the matter to the Tenancy Deposit Scheme's free dispute resolution service and submit the inventory and my photographs as evidence.

I would be grateful if you could forward a copy of this letter to Mr ⟦name|Achterberg⟧.

Yours sincerely,

⟦name|Priya Raghunathan-Cole⟧

---

A few tips:
- Attach the inventory page with photo 14 rather than just referring to it.
- Keep everything in writing. If ⟦name|Gareth⟧ rings you, follow up with a short email summarising what was said.
- You generally have 3 months from the end of the tenancy to raise a dispute with the scheme, so there's time, but don't let it drift past December.

member_id,visit_ts,club_id,door,badge_fw
⟦customer id|PF-0048213⟧,2026-09-28T06:12:44Z,COL-03,N,4.1.7
⟦customer id|PF-0049102⟧,2026-09-28T17:40:02Z,COL-03,S,4.1.7

lines 41-48 of the script:
    members = pd.read_csv(EXPORT_DIR / "members_2026-10-01.csv", dtype=str)
    visits = pd.read_csv(EXPORT_DIR / "visits_2026-09.csv", dtype=str)
    visits["visit_ts"] = pd.to_datetime(visits["visit_ts"], utc=True)
    visits = visits[visits["club_id"].isin(ACTIVE_CLUBS)]
    # TODO dedupe double door scans (fw 4.1.6 bug)
    merged = members.merge(visits, on="member_id", how="left")

Assistant: The two files don't share a column name. In the members export the key is `Member ID` (capitalised, with a space); in the visits file it's `member_id`. `merge(on="member_id")` needs that column on both sides, so pandas raises `KeyError: 'member_id'` when it looks for it in `members`.

The simplest fix is to normalise the headers right after reading:

    members.columns = (
        members.columns.str.strip()
        .str.lower()
        .str.replace(" ", "_", regex=False)
    )

After that `members` has `member_id`, `first_name`, `last_name`, `dob`, `email`, `phone`, `plan`, `home_club` and `joined`, and the merge on line 48 works as written. If you'd rather not rename everything, use `left_on="Member ID", right_on="member_id"` and drop the duplicate key column afterwards.

Two other things I noticed:

1. `Joined` is ISO (2024-01-09) but `DOB` is US-style (⟦date of birth|03/14/1991⟧). If you ever parse `dob`, pass `format="%m/%d/%Y"` explicitly, otherwise a value like ⟦date of birth|11/02/1979⟧ is ambiguous to whoever reads it later.
2. Those three member rows look like real records (⟦name|Danielle⟧'s row has a full email, phone number and birth date). If this snippet is going into a ticket or a Slack thread, swap them for generated rows, for example with Faker, before sharing.

User: lol yeah those are real, i'll delete this chat after. fixed it, thanks!! last q: my manager ⟦name|Renata⟧ wants the merged file dropped into /Volumes/PeakFit-Shared/exports/⟦username|rmatsumoto⟧/review/ every monday morning. cron or launchd?

Assistant: On macOS, launchd is the supported option. cron still works, but it needs Full Disk Access to write anything under /Volumes, which trips a lot of people up. A LaunchAgent at ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.peakfit.mergemembers.plist with `StartCalendarInterval` set to `Weekday 1, Hour 7, Minute 0` will run it every Monday at 7:00 local time.

Two caveats: a LaunchAgent only runs while you're logged in, and the share has to be mounted. Have the script check that /Volumes/PeakFit-Shared exists and write an error to a log if it doesn't, rather than silently doing nothing. And because the merged file contains birth dates and phone numbers, it's worth confirming with ⟦name|Renata⟧ who else can read that folder.

Someone opened 3 credit cards in my name. Now an email "from the credit union" wants my full SSN and a pic of my license. Legit or scam??

Throwaway because my main has my real name on it. Sorry this is long.

Two weeks ago I got a welcome letter from Meridian Peaks Federal Credit Union for a Visa Signature card I never applied for. Never banked with them, never even heard of them. Over the next 9 days: a Kohl's card, then a Lowe's card through Synchrony. Credit Karma showed 3 hard inquiries and my score dropped from 781 to 734.

What I've done so far:
- Froze Equifax, Experian and TransUnion (took about 40 min total)
- Filed at IdentityTheft.gov, report #182447391
- Police report with Lakewood PD, case 26-031877
- Called Meridian Peaks. The fraud lady (⟦name|Shonda⟧, honestly a saint) closed the card and said the application used my real SSN and real DOB but a different address, ⟦street address|4410 W 38th Ave Apt 2B, Denver, CO 80212⟧. I have never lived there. It also had my driver license number, ⟦driver license number|11-427-0938⟧, so they must have a scan of my actual license from somewhere.

Today this landed in my inbox:

> Dear Mrs. ⟦name|Halvorsen-Teague⟧,
> We are processing your fraud claim on the account ending ⟦credit card number|**** **** **** 5508⟧. To complete your identity theft affidavit we require:
> 1. Your full Social Security Number (we have ⟦ssn|XXX-XX-4471⟧ on file)
> 2. Date of birth
> 3. Front and back photo of your driver license
> Please upload within 48 hours at meridianpeaks-claims-portal.help/verify to avoid account suspension.
> Fraud Resolution Team, Meridian Peaks FCU

My SSN really does end in ⟦ssn|4471⟧. That's what's freaking me out. But the link is weird and ⟦name|Shonda⟧ told me on the phone they'd send everything by USPS.

My husband ⟦name|Arturo⟧ says just call the number on the back of my Meridian card, but I don't HAVE a Meridian card, that's the whole problem lol.

Also do I need to do anything tax-wise? I'm terrified the IRS is going to think I owe something on these.

EDIT: Thank you all. Not uploading anything. Called the number on their real website and they confirmed the email isn't from them. Forwarded it to reportphishing@apwg.org.

EDIT 2: to the person who DM'd me offering "credit repair" for $499, no.

That email is phishing. Knowing your last 4 means nothing, last-4 SSNs are in basically every breach dump. No real credit union will ever ask you to upload your full SSN to a random link with a 48-hour deadline. The deadline is the tell.

u/⟦username|CPA_in_Tucson⟧ · 5h · 640 points
On the tax question: if a creditor ever sends you a 1099-C for one of these accounts, dispute it with the creditor and keep your FTC report and police case number. You don't owe tax on debt that was never yours. Also get an IP PIN from the IRS (free, takes 10 minutes online). It stops anyone else filing a return with your SSN.

u/⟦username|mkwasniewski⟧ · 4h · 211 points
Suze Orman would tell you to freeze ChexSystems and NCTUE too, not just the big three. People forget those and then someone opens a checking account in your name.

u/⟦username|DenverDad_303⟧ · 3h · 98 points
Put that Denver address in your police report and your FTC report too. It's probably a mail drop, but if the same address shows up on other victims' applications the detectives can connect them.

1/ she gets a text "from Linkt" saying she owes $4.85 in unpaid tolls and a $185 admin fee kicks in at 5pm. link was linkt-au-paytoll[.]info. she's 74 and has literally never driven on a toll road
3:12 pm · 17 Oct 2026 · 48.2K Views

3/ the code was a CommBank one-time passcode to add a new payee. she rang me instead of reading it out (so proud of u mum). i rang the number back: straight to a generic voicemail

4/ the bit that actually scared me: he read out her address. ⟦street address|12 Banksia Cres, Glenmore Park NSW 2745⟧. correct down to the postcode. so it's not random, it's from a leak somewhere

5/ what we did, in order:
- called CommBank on 13 22 21, they locked her NetBank in about 4 mins
- reported to Scamwatch (ref SW-2026-4419087)
- forwarded the text to 7226
- changed her myGov password just in case

6/ shoutout to Dr Karl, who apparently did a whole bit on these toll scams on triple j last week that mum half-listened to in the car and it STUCK lol

7/ if your parents are in their 70s pls tell them this one sentence: nobody legit will ever ask you to read out a code they just texted you. ever. /end

Steuer-Community › Lohnsteuer & Arbeitnehmer › ELSTER / Übermittlung

Thema: Fehler 610301200 bei Übermittlung – Anlage N, Zeile 61 (Homeoffice-Pauschale)

Beitrag #1 · 14.10.2026, 21:47

Hallo zusammen,

ich verzweifle gerade an der Übermittlung unserer Einkommensteuererklärung 2025. Ich nutze die Desktop-Version (Programmversion 33.04.2391, Update vom 02.10.2026), Zusammenveranlagung, beide Arbeitnehmer, keine Kinder.

Beim Versand kommt jedes Mal:

  ERiC-Fehler 610301200: Die übermittelten Daten enthalten Fehler.
  Plausibilitätsprüfung: Anlage N (Person A), Zeile 61, Kennzahl 150 – Wert unzulässig.

In Zeile 61 steht bei mir die Tagespauschale für Homeoffice: 210 Tage × 6 € = 1.260 €. Die Höchstgrenze ist doch 1.260 €, also genau drin?! Bei meiner Frau (Person B) mit 148 Tagen = 888 € geht es ohne Probleme durch.

Was ich schon probiert habe:
– Tage auf 209 gesetzt → gleicher Fehler
– Programm neu installiert, Datenbank neu indiziert
– Belegabruf (vorausgefüllte Steuererklärung) erneut gemacht, die Lohnsteuerbescheinigung ist korrekt übernommen (Bruttoarbeitslohn 58.430,00 €, einbehaltene Lohnsteuer 9.117,00 €, Solidaritätszuschlag 0,00 €)
– Steuer-ID und Steuernummer sind korrekt eingetragen, das Finanzamt (Köln-Altstadt) stimmt auch

Hat jemand das gleiche Problem? Die Hotline sagt, Wartezeit „ca. 45 Minuten“. Die Abgabefrist war eigentlich der 31.07., ich habe aber eine Fristverlängerung bis 30.11.2026 bekommen, also noch kein Drama.

Danke vorab!

---

Antwort #2 · Moderator · 15.10.2026, 08:12

Guten Morgen,

bekanntes Problem seit Update 33.04. Kennzahl 150 wird gegen die Arbeitstage an der ersten Tätigkeitsstätte geprüft. Wenn Sie in Zeile 31 ff. für dieselben Tage auch Fahrten angegeben haben, rechnet ERiC beides zusammen und landet über der Zahl der möglichen Arbeitstage.

Workaround bis zum Patch (angekündigt als 33.05, voraussichtlich KW 43):
1. In Zeile 31 die Arbeitstage an der ersten Tätigkeitsstätte prüfen.
2. Sicherstellen, dass Homeoffice-Tage + Bürotage ≤ tatsächliche Arbeitstage laut Kalender (bei 30 Urlaubstagen sind das ca. 220–230).
3. Neu prüfen lassen (F9), dann senden.

Viele Grüße

---

Antwort #3 · Gast · 15.10.2026, 09:30

Gleicher Fehler bei mir, bei mir war es Zeile 61 + Zeile 64 gleichzeitig (Arbeitszimmer UND Tagespauschale, geht seit 2023 nicht mehr nebeneinander). Hat damals Christian Lindner als Finanzminister mit dem Jahressteuergesetz 2022 so durchgebracht.

Antwort #4 · Themenstarter · 15.10.2026, 19:05

Das war's! In Zeile 31 hatte ich 230 Bürotage stehen (aus dem Vorjahr übernommen 🙈) plus 210 Homeoffice-Tage in Zeile 61. Auf 20 Bürotage korrigiert, Übermittlung ging durch, Transferticket et7-kq2-9x4m-vb81. Bescheid kommt laut ELSTER-Postfach in ca. 6–8 Wochen.

Danke euch!

Summary:
Six hours after Ceres, the Roci's comms array is fried, Holden is asleep for once, and Amos wants to learn how to fix something without hitting it. Naomi teaches him to solder.

Notes:
For ⟦name|Imogen⟧ (⟦username|@imogen-writes-things⟧ on tumblr), who beta'd this at 2am her time and told me the middle was saggy. She was right. Any remaining saggy bits are mine.
Set loosely between seasons 3 and 4 of the show. Book canon for the Belter creole, show canon for everything else, because Cara Gee's Naomi lives in my head rent free.

Rating: Teen And Up Audiences
Archive Warning: No Archive Warnings Apply
Category: Gen
Fandom: The Expanse (TV), The Expanse - James S. A. Corey
Relationship: Naomi Nagata & Amos Burton
Characters: Naomi Nagata, Amos Burton, James Holden, Alex Kamal, Original Character(s)

The flux smelled like burnt sugar.

"You're holding it like a knife," Naomi said.

Amos looked at the iron in his fist, then at her. "That's how you hold things."

"Not this." She reached over and turned his wrist, the way you'd fix a kid's grip on a stylus. "Like a pen. You're not stabbing the board. You're asking it."

"Asking it what?"

"To let go."

Down the corridor the Roci ticked as she cooled. Alex had the con and was humming something with a slide guitar in it; Holden was, for once, actually asleep. The array had taken a fragment on the burn out of Ceres, and somewhere on the board between them was a trace no wider than a hair that had cracked clean through.

"Station I came up on," Amos said, after a while, "there was a guy. Tomas Rusk. Fixed hand terminals for the dockworkers out of a crate behind the noodle place. Never once saw him hit anything." He touched the iron to the pad and held it there too long. The pad lifted off the board like a scab. "Huh."

"That's fine," Naomi said. "Now you know where it lets go."

He looked at the ruined pad for a long moment. She waited for the joke, or the shrug, or the thing he did with his jaw when he'd decided something wasn't worth caring about.

"Rusk let me sit on the crate," Amos said instead. "Didn't charge me for it. I was maybe nine."

Naomi didn't say anything. She picked up the wick, pressed it to the pad, and drew the old solder up into the copper braid, slow, so he could see.

"Again," she said, and handed him the iron.

He held it like a pen.

THE LAST LUTEFISK SUPPER

The church basement smelled the way it had every December since 1962, which was to say like lye and coffee and the radiator Pastor Halvorsen had been promising to fix since Eisenhower.

Gran Sigrid sat at the end of the long table with her hands folded over her pocketbook, and Pete watched her watch the door.

"She's not coming," he said.

"She always comes." Sigrid didn't look at him. "Twenty-nine years Ruth Engebretsen has sat in that chair and told me my lefse was too thick."

Pete had been at the funeral in October. So had Sigrid. He didn't say that.

[... about 600 words: the supper, the Sons of Norway men arguing about the Vikings' quarterback, Pete's mother calling from Fargo, Sigrid saving a plate ...]

Assistant: I think your group leader is half right, and the half she's right about isn't the last line.

The last line works. "Too thick," said to an empty room and followed by eating the lefse anyway, is the whole story in a handful of words: grief coming out as the old argument. Keep it.

What's flat is the beat before it. "Sigrid stood, crossed the basement, and sat down in Ruth's chair" tells us exactly where we're headed, so by the time she speaks there's nothing left to discover. Two options:

1. Cut the movement and put her in the chair already: "At nine, when the last of the Sons of Norway had gone home, Pete came back from loading the car and found Gran in Ruth's chair." The reader discovers it the way Pete does.
2. Keep the movement but slow it down with one physical detail that belongs to Ruth, not Sigrid: a dent in the seat cushion, a lipstick mark on a coffee cup nobody cleared.

On names: to keep the Norwegian-Minnesotan flavor without pointing at your grandmother, try Solveig, Ingeborg, Ragnhild or Astrid. Solveig has the same rhythm as Sigrid (two syllables, stress on the first), so you won't need to rework any sentences for sound. I'd also change "since 1962" if that's the year her real church basement opened; small true details are often what makes a real person recognizable.

One practical thing: many contests ask for anonymized manuscripts, so check Bellwether's guidelines and keep your name out of the file itself, just in the submission form.

C'est une « fraude au faux RIB », malheureusement très classique dans la location. Quelques points :

1. Ce n'est pas une erreur de saisie, c'est une escroquerie : déposez plainte (commissariat ou en ligne via THESEE) et transmettez le récépissé à votre banque.
2. Demandez à votre banque un rappel de fonds pour fraude, pas une simple demande de retour : la procédure et les délais ne sont pas les mêmes.
3. Le message « correspondance partielle » vient de la vérification du bénéficiaire obligatoire depuis octobre 2025. Le fait que vous ayez validé n'empêche pas la plainte, mais la banque risque de s'en servir pour refuser un remboursement de sa poche.
4. Prévenez l'agence : leur messagerie a peut-être été piratée et d'autres locataires vont recevoir le même mail.
